plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs and small trees light up the cold season with rose-like blooms. Each flower is a ruffled cup of petals around a boss of golden stamens. The petals stand out against dark, leathery leaves, and sometimes against a dusting of winter snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March in the wild, peaking in late winter
plants.location: Japan, including coastal and woodland areas of the Japanese archipelago
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Both belong to the same genus, and Japan has prized the camellia for centuries.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems rise from clumps of strappy evergreen leaves. Each stem carries a rounded burst of trumpet-shaped flowers, like a firework frozen in blue. Along the coast it is a classic sight of high summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, December to February in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Eastern coastal South Africa, where it is native, and widely grown in gardens across the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite the common name African lily, agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words for love and flower.
